scope: F04 signed versioned desired state: an internal Go service that validates one strictly typed desired-state document, verifies its Ed25519 signature over the exact submitted payload bytes with a local operator key and keeps the accepted document as the active configuration of the running process. No HTTP, CLI or UI surface, no key generation/storage/rotation/recovery and no durable applied revision. Owner review round one on a444f05 is resolved: the active state owns its own payload copy, the verification key is copied into service-owned memory at construction, the validity window is rechecked under the state lock at acceptance time, and the accepted range of the settings is explicit deployment policy instead of a hard-coded product limit.
source_identity_algorithm: SHA-256 of sorted UTF-8 relative path + NUL + raw SHA-256(file bytes) over every tracked or untracked non-ignored file; evidence, plans/progress.json, docs/agents/SESSION_HANDOFF.json and SHA256SUMS.txt excluded because they publish this identity themselves.
core_tasks_verified: C10: internal signed versioned desired state with a strict typed document, an Ed25519 signature over the exact payload bytes using a local operator key that is separate from the mTLS trust material, a monotonic per-sensor revision and typed rejections that never replace the active configuration; process state only, no HTTP/CLI/UI and no durable applied revision
commands: go test -race -count=1 -json ./... and the discovery guard
strace -f -e trace=network over the focused C10 test binary
npm run package:web and sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS.txt inside dist/release
npm run test:clone using an isolated candidate index
Python repository, plan and source-integrity tests
npm run plan -- validate and npm run plan -- next
limitations: Remote GitHub Actions execution unverified; no push or publication.

The active configuration is process state: C10 does not persist the accepted desired state, does not change internal/storage or internal/sensor and cannot recover an applied revision after a restart. The durable applied revision and the crash convergence of an apply are C11 work.
No HTTP, CLI or UI surface, no key generation, storage, rotation or recovery, one configured verification key, no multi-signer, fleet or tenant model.

Desired-state settings semantics belong to later cards: the spool and batch ceilings follow the documented product profile, the heartbeat bounds are the C10 engineering choice, and the decoy, spool and ACK behaviour belongs to C12 to C16.

The loopback trace of the focused C10 test binary certifies that this package performs no network operation; it does not certify C13 decoy isolation, the full domain workflow, physical power-loss recovery or C30 and C40 readiness.

The local toolchain used the cached Go 1.27.2 binary directly because the ambient GOSUMDB=off setting blocks the automatic toolchain download check in this environment; the module has no external dependency, so no module download was needed.
notes: The C10 tests were written before the implementation and the first run failed because internal/config did not exist. The implementation then made them pass, and three deliberate mutations (disabling the stale revision guard, letting a stale rejection overwrite the active configuration and accepting unknown members) were each caught by the named anchor and reverted. The owner fixed the scope: only internal/config/sign.go and tests/config_signature_test.go, the fixtures and the evidence; internal/storage, internal/sensor and internal/contracts are unchanged and the durable applied revision belongs to C11.
